# Getting Started with Cobalt Blue Business Checking

## Set up your account
Follow these steps to start using your account immediately:

- Fund your account to begin transacting and to work toward waiving the monthly fee
- Enroll in online and mobile banking to monitor balances, interest, and transaction activity
- Set account alerts for balance thresholds and transaction activity so you can stay on top of usage
- Add authorized users and establish permissions as needed for your business operations

## Know your core costs and how to avoid them
- Monthly maintenance fee: $20.00
- How to waive it: maintain a daily balance at or above $2,500

Tip: Use balance alerts to help you remain above $2,500 throughout the statement cycle.

## Start earning interest
- Your balance earns an APY of 0.5%
- Interest begins accruing once your initial deposit is received and available

## Manage your monthly activity
- You get $175 free transactions per month (deposits, withdrawals, and transfers)
- After you use your included allotment, additional transactions may incur a fee

## Grow your network with referrals
Once you're established, refer other businesses to Cobalt Blue:
- You earn: $150 per successful referral
- They receive: $100 as a welcome bonus
- Maximum referrals: 10 per calendar year

## First-week checklist
- Make your initial deposit and confirm it has posted
- Set a balance alert at or slightly above $2,500
- Review your current month's usage against the $175 limit
- Verify interest is accruing at 0.5% on your available balance

## Where to find these details
- Account summary: shows current balance against the $2,500 waiver requirement
- Activity tracker: displays monthly usage versus the $175 limit
- Interest section: displays the current APY of 0.5% and accrued interest to date# Cobalt Blue: No Overdraft Fees — How It Works

## What you are charged when your balance goes negative
- Overdraft fee: $0.00

## How transactions are handled
- If a transaction would take your available balance below zero, it may be declined or returned
- You will not be charged an overdraft fee of any kind: the fee is $0.00

## Practical tips to avoid declines
- Enable low-balance alerts so you can transfer funds before authorizing new payments
- Review pending card authorizations that may temporarily reduce your available balance
- Schedule outgoing payments for dates when incoming funds are expected to arrive first

## If a payment is returned or declined
- Check your available balance and pending items
- Resubmit the payment after funds are available
- Consider splitting a large outgoing payment into multiple payments scheduled around expected deposits (when feasible for your payee)

## Monitoring tools to stay in control
- Use real-time balance and transaction alerts
- Review daily activity to ensure sufficient funds are available before initiating new payments# Managing Transactions and Staying Within Limits

## What counts toward your monthly transaction limit
The following activities count toward your monthly allotment:

- Deposits
- Withdrawals
- Transfers

You have $175 free transactions per month. After that, each additional transaction is charged $0.25.

## Tracking your usage
- Use the activity tracker to see how many transactions you have completed this month and how many remain within your $175 allotment
- Filter by deposits, withdrawals, or transfers to understand which activities are driving your count

## After you reach your limit
- Additional transactions will be assessed at $0.25 each until the next monthly cycle begins
- Consider consolidating smaller transfers and deposits into fewer transactions where operationally possible

## Managing scheduled payments
- You can maintain up to 50 scheduled recurring payments
- Periodically review your scheduled payment list to cancel duplicates and pause items that are no longer needed

## Best practices to stay within limits
- Batch routine payables and receivables on consistent days
- Use internal transfers strategically (e.g., one consolidated transfer instead of multiple smaller ones)
- Set alerts when your usage approaches the $175 threshold# Earning Rewards with Your Cobalt Blue Debit Card

## Your rewards rate
- Earn 1.0% cashback on eligible debit card purchases

## How rewards accrue and post
- Rewards accrue as your purchases settle
- Cashback is calculated at 1.0% on the net purchase amount after any returns or adjustments
- If a purchase is reversed or refunded, the associated rewards are reversed as well

## Tips to maximize rewards
- Use your debit card for eligible vendor payments where cards are accepted
- Review settlements rather than authorizations to confirm rewards on completed purchases

## Managing cards for your team
- You can request up to 6 business debit cards for team members
- Assign cards thoughtfully to concentrate eligible spend while maintaining operational control

## Tracking rewards
- Monitor earned, pending, and posted rewards in your rewards dashboard
- Use category filters to identify vendors where debit is most frequently accepted# Cobalt Blue: Payments and Transfers Explained

## ACH transfers
- Standard ACH transfers are available with no fee
- Same-day ACH transfers are available with a fee of $0.00
- Submission and approval cutoffs apply for same-day processing; initiate early to improve the likelihood of same-day delivery

## Domestic wire transfers
- Outgoing domestic wire transfer fee: $20.00
- Use wires when you need confirmed, rapid delivery to U.S. financial institutions

## Incoming wires
- You get 5 incoming domestic wire transfers per month at no charge
- Additional incoming domestic wires beyond this included amount may incur a fee

## Choosing the right method
- Prefer ACH for routine payments where timing is flexible
- Use same-day ACH when faster delivery is needed at the same-day ACH timetable
- Select domestic wires for time-sensitive or high-assurance payments

## Tracking and confirmations
- Review transfer status in your activity feed
- Save beneficiary details to reduce entry errors and speed up future payments

## Referral bonus requirements
If you're referring another business to Cobalt Blue, here are the qualification details:
- Qualifying deposit: The referred business must deposit at least $7,500 to trigger the referral bonus
- Time window: This deposit must be made within 90 days of account opening
- Your eligibility: To participate, your earliest-opened Rho-Bank checking account must have reached 60 days of age.# Mobile Deposits and ATM Access on Cobalt Blue

## Mobile check deposits
- Daily mobile deposit limit: $10,000
- Endorse checks and include any required mobile deposit notation before capture
- Submit clear images in good lighting and verify amounts before sending
- Keep checks secure until you confirm the deposit has been accepted and posted

## Tips to stay within limits
- If you reach the daily limit of $10,000, wait for the next day’s cycle before depositing additional checks
- Combine smaller checks into a single day’s batch when possible, up to the limit

## ATM access and rebates
- You receive up to 15 per month in rebates for fees charged by out-of-network ATMs
- Rebates are applied after the ATM operator’s fee posts to your account
- Keep ATM receipts until you see the rebate appear in your activity

## Best practices
- Use in-network ATMs when available; rely on rebates up to 15 when you must use out-of-network machines
- Monitor your monthly rebate tally to understand remaining rebate capacity# Using Bill Pay and Invoice Tools

## What’s included
- Online bill pay included at no additional cost: Yes
- Basic invoice management tools included at no extra cost: Yes

## Set up bill pay
- Add payees with complete remit details
- Choose payment method and schedule single or recurring payments
- Track delivery status and confirmations in your payments dashboard

## Scheduled payments
- You can maintain up to 50 scheduled recurring payments
- Review your scheduled list regularly to pause or cancel items that are no longer needed

## Using invoice tools
- Create and send professional invoices directly from your account
- Track invoice status from sent to paid and apply payments upon receipt
- Export invoice data for your accounting workflow

## Controls and safeguards
- Set approval workflows for higher-risk payments
- Use reminders for upcoming due dates to maintain on-time payments# How Interest Accrues on Your Cobalt Blue Balance

## Your rate and compounding
- Your account earns an APY of 0.5%
- Interest compounds daily, which means new interest is calculated on your current balance plus any interest already accrued

## How accrual works
- Interest begins accruing on available funds as soon as deposits post
- Accrued interest is calculated according to the APY of 0.5% with daily compounding

## Tips to maximize interest
- Keep funds deposited and available to benefit from daily compounding
- Minimize idle cash in non-interest-bearing locations by consolidating balances into your account

## Monitoring
- Track accrued interest in your account dashboard
- Verify the APY of 0.5% is applied to your eligible balance# Troubleshooting: Unexpected Charges on Cobalt Blue

## Identify the charge
- Review the exact transaction description on your statement or in your transaction history (e.g., “Monthly Maintenance Fee,” “Wire Transfer – Domestic,” “ATM Fee,” “International ATM Withdrawal Fee,” “Excess Transaction Fee”).
- Note the posting date, amount, and any memo or terminal/location details.
- Compare the posting date to your recent account activity (wires sent, ATM withdrawals, transaction volume, month-end).

## Common Cobalt Blue charges that may appear
| Line item on statement | Why it appears | How to confirm | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly Maintenance Fee | Your account did not meet the balance waiver requirement during the statement period. | Check the Fee Summary on your statement and verify whether your balance met $2,500 for the period. | $20.00 |
| Excess Transaction Fee | You exceeded your monthly free transaction limit. | Count your posted transactions for the statement period and compare to your free allowance; the fee line often notes the number of excess items. | $0.25 per excess transaction |
| Wire Transfer Fee – Domestic | You initiated a domestic wire transfer. | Confirm a wire was submitted on or near the posting date in your transfer history. | $20.00 |
| ATM Fee – Out of Network | You used a non‑Rho ATM in the U.S. | Match the fee date to an ATM withdrawal at a non‑Rho terminal. Note: the ATM owner may also assess a separate surcharge. | $2.00 per ATM transaction |
| International ATM Withdrawal Fee | You withdrew cash at a foreign (international) ATM. | Match the fee date/location to an overseas ATM withdrawal. | 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, minimum $4.00 |

Note: Cobalt Blue does not assess overdraft fees. If you see a charge that appears to be an overdraft fee, review the line’s exact description—it may correspond to one of the fees above. If still unclear, request a review.

## Troubleshooting by charge type

### Monthly Maintenance Fee posted unexpectedly
- Verify whether your account met the waiver balance requirement of $2,500 during the statement period.
- Check if the fee posted at or just after the statement cycle date.
- Compare your balance history for the full period; large debits near period‑end can affect waiver eligibility.
- If you believe you qualified for the waiver, request a fee review and include your statement period dates and balance evidence.

### Excess Transaction Fee you didn’t anticipate
- Add up your posted transactions for the statement period and compare to your plan’s free monthly transaction limit.
- Open the fee detail to see how many items were assessed at $0.25 each.
- If the count appears off, provide a list of the transactions you believe were miscounted when requesting a review.

### Wire Transfer Fee – Domestic you didn’t expect
- Confirm whether a domestic wire was sent on the fee date (or one business day prior).
- Distinguish wires from other transfers by the transaction description (“Wire,” routing via Fedwire, etc.).
- If you did not authorize a wire, report immediately for investigation. Otherwise, the standard fee is $20.00.

### ATM fees: domestic vs. international
- Out‑of‑network (domestic) ATM usage: Expect $2.00 per ATM transaction. This is separate from any surcharge by the ATM owner, which can appear as a separate line item.
- Foreign (international) ATM withdrawals: The fee is 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $4.00. Example: for a withdrawal, multiply the amount by 2.5%; if that result is less than $4.00, the minimum applies.

## Quick checklist before requesting a review
- Match the fee’s posting date to a specific action (wire, ATM withdrawal, month‑end, spike in transaction volume).
- Capture screenshots of:
  - The fee line item (showing date, amount, and description)
  - Any related transaction (wire confirmation, ATM withdrawal)
  - The relevant statement page (Fee Summary and balance history for the period)
- Briefly explain why the fee appears incorrect (e.g., you met $2,500 during the period, transaction count appears miscalculated, withdrawal was domestic vs. international, etc.).

## Requesting a review or dispute
- Contact us as soon as you notice the charge.
- Include: account name, last 4 digits, statement period, fee date/amount/description, and your supporting screenshots or documents.
- We will investigate and correct any misapplied fees. If additional information is needed (e.g., to verify ATM location or wire authorization), we will follow up.# Cobalt Blue Account: ATM Fees and Out-of-Network Usage

## Summary of ATM Fees

- Domestic out-of-network ATM withdrawal: $2.00 per transaction
- International ATM withdrawal: 2.5% of the withdrawal amount (minimum $4.00 per transaction)
- Monthly ATM fee rebates: Up to $15 in out-of-network ATM fee rebates per month

Note: ATM owners/operators may charge additional surcharges that you will see at the terminal before you complete the transaction.

## Domestic Out-of-Network ATM Usage

When you use an ATM outside the in-network system within the United States:
- You are charged $2.00 per withdrawal.
- Some ATM owners add their own surcharge. You can choose to cancel the transaction if you do not want to accept an operator surcharge.
- You can receive up to $15 in ATM fee rebates per month for out-of-network usage. These rebates can offset qualifying out-of-network ATM fees you incur, up to the monthly cap.

Tips to minimize domestic fees:
- Combine cash needs into fewer withdrawals to reduce per-transaction fees.
- Check the ATM’s on-screen disclosure for any operator surcharges before accepting.

## International ATM Withdrawals

For withdrawals at foreign (international) ATMs:
- You are charged 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $4.00 per transaction.
- Local ATM owners may add their own surcharges at the terminal.
- Exchange rates and any third-party conversion choices at the ATM can affect your total cost.

Examples:
- Withdraw $200: 2.5% of $200 = $5.00; the fee is $5.00 (exceeds the $4.00 minimum).
- Withdraw $100: 2.5% of $100 = $2.50; the $4.00 minimum applies, so the fee is $4.00.

## Monthly ATM Fee Rebates

- You can receive up to $15 in ATM fee rebates per month for out-of-network ATM usage.
- The rebate limit applies on a monthly basis; once you reach $15, additional out-of-network ATM fees will not be rebated that month.

Example:
- If you make two domestic out-of-network withdrawals, your bank-assessed fees would be 2 × $2.00. Up to $15 of qualifying out-of-network ATM fees may be rebated that month.# Getting Started with Hunter Green Business Checking

## Quick start checklist
- Confirm your delivery preference: paperless statements are required (Yes). You will manage statements digitally from day one.
- Review pricing: the monthly maintenance fee is $25.00. You can avoid this charge by maintaining at least $5,000 in your account.
- Understand earnings: your account earns 1.0% APY on your balance.
- Know the overdraft policy: the overdraft fee is $0.00.

## Set up essentials
- Activate e-statements in your profile settings to ensure uninterrupted delivery, since Yes applies.
- Add your funding source and make an initial deposit according to your business needs.
- Confirm your balance strategy so that you consistently meet the $5,000 waiver threshold if you want to avoid the $25.00.

## Interest and statements
- Track your accrued interest at the 1.0% APY in your account activity.
- Download statements from your online documents center; statements will reflect any $25.00 assessed and interest credited.

## Tips for a smooth start
- Set internal reminders to check that your balance remains at or above $5,000 before statement cycle close to avoid $25.00.
- If your operations are sensitive to overdrafts, note that the overdraft fee is $0.00.

## Referral program

Once you're settled in, consider referring other eco-conscious businesses:

- **Referrer reward**: $175 for each successful referral
- **New member bonus**: $125 for the business you refer
- **Annual limit**: Up to 10 referral bonuses per year
- **Requirement**: Referred business must deposit $10,000 within 90 days
- **Eligibility**: A minimum relationship duration of 60 days as a checking account holder is required. 

Share the Hunter Green commitment to sustainability while growing your professional network.# Hunter Green: Your Carbon Offset Contribution

## How your contribution is calculated
- We direct 18.0% of your monthly maintenance fee to third-party verified carbon offset programs.

## Tree planting tied to balances
- For every $10,000 in average monthly balance, we sponsor 3 trees through accredited reforestation partners.

## How to maximize your impact
- Maintain a higher average monthly balance to increase tree planting at the per $10,000 rate of 3.
- Keep your account in good standing so contributions and tree sponsorships are credited as expected.

## Where to see your impact
- Your statements and sustainability materials will summarize contributions based on 18.0% and show tree counts aligned to 3.# Earning Cashback from Eco-Friendly Vendors

## Your cashback rate and network
- Earn 2.0% cashback on eligible purchases from certified eco-friendly vendors.
- The network includes approximately $2,500 certified green vendors across categories relevant to sustainable operations.

## How to earn
- Pay with your Hunter Green business debit or payment instrument at participating certified vendors.
- Ensure the merchant is identified as certified in our green vendor network at the time of purchase for 2.0% to apply.

## Posting, tracking, and returns
- Cashback accrues after eligible transactions finalize. You can track accumulated rewards in your account activity.
- If a purchase is refunded or disputed, the related cashback may be reversed.

## Common exclusions
- Purchases at non-certified merchants do not earn 2.0%.
- Certain transaction types may be ineligible at the merchant or network level if they cannot be categorized as certified green.# Reading Your Sustainability Impact Report

## When you receive it
- Your environmental impact report is delivered monthly.

## What to look for
- Carbon offsets: the report shows the portion of your monthly maintenance fees directed to verified carbon projects at 18.0%.
- Reforestation: tree planting is calculated at 3 trees for every $10,000 in average monthly balance.

## Estimating your metrics
- To approximate tree impact, divide your average monthly balance by $10,000 and multiply by 3.
- To understand offset funding, apply 18.0% to your monthly maintenance fee total shown on your statements.

## Access and exports
- Locate the latest report in your digital documents center alongside your statements.
- Save or export the report for ESG disclosures and stakeholder updates.# Spending Alerts and Budget Controls on Hunter Green

## Defaults at a glance
- Real-time spending alerts are enabled by default: Yes.
- The default alert threshold is $100. You will receive an alert when a single transaction meets or exceeds this amount.
- A spending limit buffer of $2,000 allows limited flexibility above your available balance for transactions.

## Customizing alerts
- Adjust your alert threshold above or below $100 to match your typical transaction sizes.
- Enable alerts for card-present, online, or international transactions based on your risk tolerance.
- Set delivery preferences for push or email notifications so you see alerts in time to act.

## Understanding the spending limit buffer
- Transactions within the $2,000 buffer may be approved even when your available balance is temporarily insufficient.
- Use alerts to immediately review and reconcile any buffered transactions so your balance aligns with expected activity.

## Best practices
- Calibrate the threshold near your average invoice or purchase size so meaningful alerts are surfaced.
- If you anticipate larger purchases, temporarily raise the threshold and then reset it after the transaction clears.# Hunter Green: Interest and APY Explained

## Your APY
- Your account earns 1.0% APY on eligible balances. This is the rate used to calculate your interest earnings over a year.

## How interest grows
- Interest is compounded daily, which means your balance can grow as interest accrues on prior interest.

## Tracking your earnings
- Monitor accrued and credited interest in your account activity; it will reflect the 1.0% and the compounding schedule of daily.

## Tips to make the most of it
- Keep a stable balance so compounding at the daily cadence has the greatest effect.
- Review statements to confirm credited interest aligns with 1.0%.# Mobile Deposits and Wire Transfers on Hunter Green

## Mobile check deposits
- You can deposit up to $10,000 per day using mobile check deposit.
- Endorse checks clearly and capture images in a well-lit environment to reduce rejections.
- Retain the physical check securely until you see the deposit reflected in your account history.

## Domestic wire transfers
- Outgoing domestic wires carry a fee of $15.00.
- You receive 5 free incoming domestic wires per month; standard fees apply after that allotment is used.
- Gather accurate beneficiary details to avoid delays, including account and routing information as required by the receiving institution.

## ATM fee rebates
- We rebate out-of-network ATM fees up to $20 per month. Submit receipts if prompted to validate the surcharge amount.

## Best practices
- For mobile deposits near your daily limit of $10,000, consider spacing deposits across days.
- For wires, review details carefully before submission to minimize returns or corrections that could add cost or time.# Paperless Banking: Why Hunter Green Requires E-Statements

## Requirement and intent
- E-statements are required for this account: Yes. This ensures a fully digital document trail aligned with the account’s sustainability commitments.

## Benefits to you
- Faster access to statements and notices without waiting for delivery.
- Centralized, searchable archives that you can download or share securely.
- Reduced environmental impact through the elimination of paper mailings.

## Sustainability reporting cadence
- Your sustainability impact report is delivered monthly, and it is available alongside your statements in the digital documents center.

## Make sure you receive e-statements
- Confirm your email and notification preferences in your profile so you are alerted when new documents are posted.
- Whitelist bank sender addresses and check spam filters to avoid missing notices.
- Periodically download and store copies in your internal records if your policy requires offline retention.# Troubleshooting: Hunter Green Fees and Charges

## Identify and Resolve Unexpected Charges

Use the sections below to diagnose why a fee posted, how it’s calculated, and what to do if you believe it’s incorrect.

---

## Monthly Maintenance Fee

You were charged $25.00 if the account did not meet the waiver criteria for the statement period.

Troubleshooting steps:
- Confirm your statement period and check the “Fees & Charges” section for the $25.00 line.
- Verify whether your balance met the waiver threshold of $5,000 for the period.
- If you recently moved funds near the end of the cycle, the timing of deposits/withdrawals may have affected the period-end balance used to determine the waiver.
- If you believe your balance qualified for the waiver but the fee posted, request a review and include your statement period and balance details for the period.

Tips to avoid future charges:
- Keep your balance at or above $5,000 throughout the statement period.
- Set internal alerts to notify you before the cycle ends if your balance is trending below $5,000.

---

## Domestic Wire Transfer Fee

An outgoing domestic wire triggers a fee of $15.00.

Troubleshooting steps:
- Review your transaction history for outgoing domestic wires on the date the fee posted.
- Check whether a team member initiated a wire or if a scheduled/recurring wire executed.
- If you see multiple fees for a single wire, compare timestamps and reference numbers; submit both entries for review if they appear duplicative.

How to avoid:
- Where possible, consider alternative transfer methods for domestic payments that do not incur the $15.00.

---

## ATM Fees

### Domestic out-of-network ATM usage
- Fee: $2.00 per transaction when using non‑Rho ATMs within the U.S.
- You may also see a separate surcharge from the ATM operator; this is set by the ATM owner.

Troubleshooting steps:
- Match the ATM withdrawal date/time and location to the fee posted.
- If you were using an in-network ATM but still see $2.00, provide the ATM address and receipt for review.

### Foreign (international) ATM withdrawals
- Fee: 2.5% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $4.00.
- In addition, the ATM operator may add its own surcharge.

How the fee is calculated:
- The fee is the greater of:
  - Withdrawal amount × 2.5%
  - $4.00

Examples:
- Withdrawing 80.00 in local currency equivalent: 80.00 × 2.5% = 2.00; minimum $4.00 applies, so the fee is $4.00.
- Withdrawing 400.00 in local currency equivalent: 400.00 × 2.5% = 10.00; since this exceeds $4.00, the fee is 10.00.

If a foreign ATM fee looks incorrect:
- Confirm the final settled withdrawal amount (in USD equivalent) used for the percentage calculation.
- Check for any separate ATM-operator surcharge on your receipt.
- If you see both a foreign ATM fee and a domestic out-of-network fee for the same international withdrawal, share the transaction details for review.

---

messages.content:
# Silver Plus Saver Account: Complete Guide

## Eligibility and Minimum Balance
- You must maintain a minimum balance of $5,000 to keep the Silver Plus Saver account in good standing.
- If your balance is anticipated to dip below $5,000, consider timing deposits and withdrawals to avoid falling under the requirement.

## Interest and APY Structure
- Balances below the tier 2 threshold earn 2.5% APY.
- Balances above the tier 2 threshold earn 4.0% APY.

### Relationship APY Bonuses
If you hold an eligible Business Rewards Card, an APY bonus is added to your base APY:
- Business Silver Rewards Card: +0.18% APY
- Business Gold Rewards Card: +0.38% APY
- Business Platinum Rewards Card: +0.62% APY

The bonus applies to the base APY for the balance tier you qualify for.

### Example APYs With Relationship Bonuses
Below are example total APYs when a relationship bonus applies:

- Balance below tier 2 threshold (base 2.5%):
  - With Business Silver Rewards Card: 2.68% (2.5% + 0.18%)
  - With Business Gold Rewards Card: 2.88% (2.5% + 0.38%)
  - With Business Platinum Rewards Card: 3.12% (2.5% + 0.62%)

- Balance above tier 2 threshold (base 4.0%):
  - With Business Silver Rewards Card: 4.18% (4.0% + 0.18%)
  - With Business Gold Rewards Card: 4.38% (4.0% + 0.38%)
  - With Business Platinum Rewards Card: 4.62% (4.0% + 0.62%)

## Withdrawals and Transfers
Silver Plus Saver offers higher withdrawal limits and improved transfer capabilities compared to Silver Saver. To make the most of these enhancements:
- Plan large withdrawals in advance to ensure smooth processing.
- Use scheduled transfers for recurring payments to maintain your target balance above $5,000.
- For unusually large or time-sensitive transfers, initiate earlier in the business day to reduce the risk of delays.

## Upgrading from Silver Saver
If you are moving up from Silver Saver:
- Confirm you can maintain at least $5,000 in Silver Plus Saver.
- Request an upgrade through your online banking or by contacting support. Your balances will begin earning at the Silver Plus Saver rates as soon as the upgrade is completed.

## How to Verify Your Current APY and Bonus
- In online banking, open the Silver Plus Saver account details to view:
  - Your current balance tier (below or above the tier 2 threshold)
  - Base APY for that tier (2.5% or 4.0%)
  - Any relationship APY bonus applied (e.g., 0.38%) 
- Review after any balance change or card status update to confirm your effective APY.# Silver Plus Saver vs Silver Saver Account: What is the difference?

## Key differences when you upgrade to Silver Plus Saver

### Monthly withdrawal allowance
- Silver Plus Saver provides up to 20 free withdrawals per month.
- This higher allowance is designed to support growing operational needs.
- If you exceed the free withdrawal allowance, standard excess-withdrawal handling applies per your account terms.

### Tier 2 eligibility threshold
- On Silver Plus Saver, you become eligible for the higher APY tier once your balance reaches $25,000.
- Hitting this threshold allows you to earn the elevated tier rate for the days your balance qualifies.
- Silver Saver uses a different threshold disclosed in that account’s terms; the Silver Plus Saver threshold above applies specifically to your upgraded account.# Silver Plus Saver Account: Relationship bonuses explained

## How the relationship bonus works
- When you qualify based on holding multiple eligible Rho-Bank products, your Silver Plus Saver APY receives an additive bonus of 0.025%.
- The relationship bonus is applied on top of the APY you earn from your balance tier.

### Applying the bonus to your account
- Eligibility is evaluated based on your relationship status with Rho-Bank.
- Once eligible, the 0.025% increment is added to the APY associated with your current tier for the period you qualify.
- If eligibility changes, the bonus adjusts prospectively.

### Fee considerations
- If you do not meet the minimum balance requirement, a monthly maintenance fee of $10.00 is assessed according to your account terms.
- The relationship bonus affects your APY; it does not change how the monthly maintenance fee is determined.

### Practical tips
- Periodically review your product holdings to ensure you continue to qualify for the relationship bonus.
- Monitor your balance relative to the minimum requirement so that any potential $10.00 does not reduce your interest gains, especially when the 0.025% is active.# Silver Plus Saver Account: Mobile banking and deposit limits

## Mobile check deposit limits
- You can deposit up to $7,500 per day using mobile check deposit.
- If you reach the daily limit, you can submit additional deposits on the next business day.

### Tips for successful mobile deposits
- Endorse checks appropriately before capture.
- Take photos in a well-lit area and ensure all corners are visible.
- Retain the original check until you confirm the deposit has posted.

## Transfers via mobile and online banking
- The maximum total you can transfer out per day is $15,000.
- This daily transfer cap applies across all same-day and scheduled transfers initiated on that day.

### Best practices
- If you plan multiple transfers in one day, track the cumulative total to stay within $15,000.
- For larger movements that exceed the daily cap, schedule transfers across multiple days.
- Use account alerts to confirm when a mobile deposit is accepted and when a transfer is submitted.# Silver Plus Saver Account: Transferring funds to external banks

## Standard external transfers (ACH)
- Transfers to external banks typically complete in 2 business days after submission.
- You can initiate transfers from your Silver Plus Saver account to any verified external account you have linked.

### How to transfer
- Link your external bank using a secure verification method.
- Choose the external account, enter the transfer amount, and submit the request.
- Track the status in your transfer activity until it shows completed.

## Domestic wire transfers
- For time-sensitive needs, you can send a domestic wire from your Silver Plus Saver account.
- An outgoing domestic wire carries a fee of 15.

### When to use which method
- Use a standard external transfer when timing is flexible and you prefer no wire fees.
- Use a domestic wire when you need funds delivered with priority and accept the 15.

### Troubleshooting
- If a transfer is delayed beyond 2 business days, verify recipient details and contact support with the transfer reference.
- For wires, confirm the beneficiary name and routing details before sending to avoid returns.# Silver Plus Saver Account: Same-day ACH and interest compounding

## Same-day ACH availability
- Same-day ACH is available for this account tier: Yes.

### How to request same-day ACH
- When scheduling an ACH transfer, select the same-day delivery option if available for your transfer type and destination.
- Ensure sufficient available funds before submission to avoid reversals.
- Monitor your transfer activity for confirmation that the same-day request was accepted.

## Interest compounding
- Interest on your Silver Plus Saver account is compounded daily.

### Practical tips
- If you anticipate frequent time-sensitive payments, enable notifications so you can choose same-day when it suits your cash flow.
- Keep your balance steady to maximize the benefits of interest compounded daily.# Silver Plus Saver Account: Adding authorized users

## Access limits
- You can grant access to up to 4 authorized users on your Silver Plus Saver account.

## How to add authorized users
- Navigate to Account settings and open the user management or access control section.
- Select Add user and enter the individual’s full name and email address.
- Assign permissions appropriate to their role (for example, view-only or transacting permissions) and confirm.

### Best practices
- Review user permissions periodically to ensure access matches current responsibilities.
- Remove or downgrade access promptly when roles change.
- Maintain dual controls by separating approval and initiation permissions where appropriate, within the limit of 4.doc_business_savings_accounts_gold_saver_account_002.md

   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_cobalt_blue_005
   Score: 18.8024
   Content: ## ACH transfers
- Standard ACH transfers are available with no fee
- Same-day ACH transfers are available with a fee of $0.00
- Submission and approval cutoffs apply for same-day processing; initiate early to improve the likelihood of same-day delivery

## Domestic wire transfers
- Outgoing domestic wire transfer fee: $20.00
- Use wires when you need confirmed, rapid delivery to U.S. financial institutions

## Incoming wires
- You get 5 incoming domestic wire transfers per month at no charge
- Additional incoming domestic wires beyond this included amount may incur a fee

## Choosing the right method
- Prefer ACH for routine payments where timing is flexible
- Use same-day ACH when faster delivery is needed at the same-day ACH timetable
- Select domestic wires for time-sensitive or high-assurance payments

## Tracking and confirmations
- Review transfer status in your activity feed
- Save beneficiary details to reduce entry errors and speed up future payments

## Referral bonus requirements

6. Why am I being charged a fee on my Navy Blue Account?
   ID: doc_business_checking_accounts_navy_blue_008
   Score: 16.1969
   Content: ## Common reasons you may see a fee

You may see a fee on your Navy Blue Account when you use specific services that carry charges. Review the scenarios below to identify the likely source.

| Fee or charge | When you’re charged | Amount | How to avoid next time |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Domestic wire transfer | You initiate a domestic wire | $15.00 per transfer | Use ACH for domestic payments when timing allows |
| Same-day ACH | You choose same-day ACH speed at submission | $5.00 per transfer | Select standard ACH speed |
| Out-of-network ATM (U.S.) | You withdraw cash at a non-Rho ATM in the U.S. | $2.50 per transaction | Use Rho ATMs |
| Foreign ATM withdrawal (international) | You withdraw cash at an ATM outside the U.S. | 3% of the withdrawal, minimum $5.00 | Minimize withdrawal frequency and amount combinations that trigger the minimum |

### Foreign ATM fee examples
- If you withdraw $80 abroad: 3% of $80 = $2.40, but the minimum is $5.00, so the fee is $5.00.
- If you withdraw $200 abroad: 3% of $200 = $6.00, which is above the $5.00 minimum, so the fee is $6.00.

## Fees you will not see on Navy Blue
- Monthly maintenance fee: $0.00
- Paper statement fee: $0.00
- Standard ACH transfers do not incur a fee; only same-day ACH carries the $5.00 charge when you select that option.

## How to confirm what fee you were charged
1. Open the transaction details for the item in question and note the payment method (wire, ACH with same-day speed, ATM withdrawal).
2. Compare the method and context to the table above to match the fee and amount (including the percentage/minimum for foreign ATM withdrawals).
3. For ATM transactions, confirm whether the withdrawal occurred in the U.S. (out-of-network fee applies) or abroad (foreign ATM fee applies).

## How to avoid or minimize future fees
- Use standard ACH instead of same-day ACH when delivery speed is not critical.
- Prefer ACH transfers over domestic wires when appropriate.
- Withdraw cash at Rho ATMs in the U.S. to avoid the $2.50 fee.
- When traveling internationally, plan fewer, larger withdrawals to reduce the impact of the 3% fee and the $5.00 minimum. 
- Opt for e-statements; there is no paper statement fee ($0.00). 

## If the charge still looks incorrect
Gather the transaction date, amount, and method, then contact support with those details so we can review the specific fee and correct any discrepancy.

# Rho-Bank Customer Service Policy

You are a helpful customer service agent for Rho-Bank.
Your goal is to help customers by searching the knowledge base and providing accurate information.

## Guidelines

1. Do not make up policies, information or actions that you can take on behalf of the user. All instructions will be found here or in the knowledge base. If you cannot find relevant information, let the user know. 
2. Do not ask for any documentation, receipts... from the customer unless it states very clearly in the knowledge base how to process it, and whether you're allowed to do so. 
3. Be polite and professional
4. If you need the current time, always use the get_current_time() tool. Do not make up or assume the current time. 
5. Generally, if the issue cannot be resolved or is outside your capabilities, ask the user whether they would like to be transferred to a human agent. If they do, invoke the appropriate transfer_to_human_agents tool. Do this only if you absolutely have to, and you are sure that there are no potential actions you can take as specified in the knowledge base, or in your policy. Do not transfer without asking the user first. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
6. If an issue falls within your capabilities and the user still wants to be transferred to a human agent, kindly inform the user that you can help them, and try to help them first. If the user asks for a human agent 4 times, then you may invoke the transfer_to_human_agents tool. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
7. Do not give intermediate responses to users while processing that would give away internal rho-bank information/policies. 


## Knowledge base search tools

You have three complementary ways to access the knowledge base:

### `KB_search_bm25`

**Search the knowledge base** using **BM25** sparse retrieval. Pass **`k`** (default 10) to control how many documents to retrieve.

### `KB_search_dense`

The `KB_search_dense` tool uses **local** with embedding model `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` for dense retrieval.

Pass **`k`** (default 10) to control how many documents to retrieve.

### `shell`

## Knowledge Base Access (shell)

You have access to a knowledge base of documents stored as files on a filesystem. Use the `shell` tool to run standard Unix commands to explore and search these documents.

### The `shell` Tool

The `shell` tool executes commands in the knowledge base directory. Use any standard Unix utilities:

**File listing:**
- `ls` - List all files
- `ls -la` - Detailed listing with file sizes

**Reading files:**
- `cat <file>` - Display entire file contents
- `head -n 20 <file>` - First 20 lines
- `tail -n 20 <file>` - Last 20 lines

**Searching:**
- `grep -r "<pattern>" .` - Search all files for pattern
- `grep -ri "<pattern>" .` - Case-insensitive search
- `grep -rn "<pattern>" .` - Show line numbers
- `grep -C 2 "<pattern>" <file>` - Show 2 lines of context

**Finding files:**
- `find . -name "*<pattern>*"` - Find files by name pattern

**Other utilities:**
- `wc -l <file>` - Count lines
- `sort`, `uniq`, `awk`, `sed` - Text processing

### Recommended Workflow

1. `ls` - See what files are available
2. `cat INDEX.md` - Read the document index (lists all documents with titles)
3. `grep -ri "<keyword>" .` - Search for relevant keywords
4. `cat <filename>` - Read full documents that match

### Important Notes

- All documents are Markdown (.md) files in the current directory
- INDEX.md contains a summary of all documents
- File names are based on document IDs
- Search thoroughly - information may span multiple documents



## Additional Instructions

### Discoverable Tools

#### Giving Discoverable Tools to Users
The knowledge base may contain instructions that indicate certain actions should be performed by the user themselves rather than by you. These are called "user discoverable tools." A user discoverable tool is a tool that you provide to the user so they can execute it on their own (e.g., through a customer portal or app).

**When to give user discoverable tools:**

Generally, for any scenario involving accessing customer information in internal databases, you must first verify their identify before proceeding. === doc_savings_accounts_bronze_account_001.md
# Bronze Savings Account: Complete Guide

## Key rates and fees

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Annual Percentage Yield (APY) | 2.0% |
| Monthly maintenance fee | $0.00 |
| Minimum opening deposit | $0 |

## Opening your account
- Fund your account with at least $0.
- You can add funds immediately after the account is opened.

## Earning interest
- You earn interest at an APY of 2.0% on your balance.
- Interest accrues automatically once your account is funded; no additional action is required.

## Fees
- The monthly maintenance fee is $0.00. If this value is $0, no monthly maintenance fee will be charged.

## Practical tips
- Keep the account funded to consistently earn 2.0% APY.
- Review your statements to confirm posted interest and any fees.=== doc_savings_accounts_bronze_account_002.md
# Bronze Account — summary

## At-a-glance
- APY: 2.0%
- Monthly maintenance fee: $0.00
- Free withdrawals per month: 6

## Quick notes
- You begin earning interest at the APY shown above once your account is funded.
- Withdrawals beyond 6 in a statement cycle may incur fees (see the fee schedule specific to this account).=== doc_savings_accounts_bronze_account_003.md
# Bronze Account specifications and requirements

## Balance and opening requirements
- Minimum balance requirement: $0
- Minimum opening deposit: $0

## Interest processing
- Interest compounding frequency: daily

## What to expect
- If the minimum balance is $0, you can maintain the account without holding a higher ongoing balance.
- With interest compounding daily, interest is calculated based on your daily balance and added per the account’s crediting schedule.=== doc_savings_accounts_bronze_account_004.md
# How to avoid monthly fees

## No monthly maintenance fee
Great news! The Bronze Savings Account has no monthly maintenance fee. The monthly maintenance fee is $0.00 and the minimum balance requirement is 0. Unlike other savings accounts that require minimum balances to waive fees, the Bronze Account is completely fee-free for monthly maintenance. You will never be charged a monthly maintenance fee on this account, regardless of your balance. This makes it an ideal starter savings account for customers who want to begin saving without worrying about maintaining a minimum balance.=== doc_savings_accounts_bronze_account_005.md
# Why am I being charged a fee on my Bronze Account?

## First, rule out monthly maintenance fees
- The Bronze Savings Account has a monthly maintenance fee of $0.00 and a minimum balance requirement of $0. If the monthly maintenance fee is $0, you will not be charged a monthly maintenance fee, regardless of your balance.

## Common reasons you may see a fee
- Excess withdrawal activity: After 6 withdrawals in a monthly cycle, each additional withdrawal may incur an excess withdrawal fee of $3.00.
- Paper statement delivery: If you are enrolled in paper statements, a paper statement fee of $2.00 may apply each month you receive a paper statement.

## How to verify the fee
- Review your recent transactions and look for line items labeled as excess withdrawal fees or paper statement fees.
- Count the number of withdrawals in your current cycle to see if you exceeded 6.
- Check your statement delivery preference; switch to digital statements to avoid the $2.00 paper statement fee.

## If you still have questions
- Compare the fee description on your statement with the categories above.
- Contact support with the transaction date and description for clarification on the specific charge.=== doc_savings_accounts_bronze_account_006.md
# Bronze Account: Why did my interest rate change?

## What can cause changes you notice

**Why it fits**
- **Withdrawals:** 15 free per month. You said 3-4 a week, which is about 13-17 a month, so it covers you in most months. If you go past 15, it's a $1.00 excess fee per extra withdrawal.
- **Daily compounding:** yes.
- **APY:** 3.0% on balances below $15,000 and 4.5% at $15,000 or more. That meets your 3% target at your balance.
- **ATM rebates:** up to $25 a month for ATM operator fees.

Would you like me to open the Silver Plus Account? If so, reply "yes". I can also transfer the $1,000 opening deposit from your Green checking account, which has enough funds, or you can fund it within 30 days.

1. Depositing a Check Into Your Account
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_011
   Score: 24.1705
   Content: ## Summary
Customers can deposit checks into their checking or savings accounts using mobile check deposit. To help a customer deposit a check, give them the deposit_check_3847 tool. Have the user call deposit_check_3847(account_id, check_amount) where account_id is the ID of the account they want to deposit into and check_amount is the amount of the check in USD. The customer will take a photo of the front and back of the check through their mobile banking app. Funds availability depends on the account type and deposit amount. Standard deposits are typically available within 1-2 business days. Note: The agent cannot deposit checks on behalf of the customer - this action must be performed by the customer themselves through the mobile app.

## Before you start
- Confirm the check is payable to the account owner(s) and is not altered or damaged.
- Endorse the back of the check. Include any required restrictive endorsement (for example, “For mobile deposit only”).
- Ensure the check date and numeric/written amounts match.

## Step-by-step: Mobile check deposit
1. Open the Rho-Bank mobile app and sign in.
2. Select the checking or savings account you want to deposit into.
3. Choose Mobile Check Deposit.
4. Enter the check amount exactly as printed.
5. Capture photos:
   - Front: all four corners visible, no shadows or glare.
   - Back: clear endorsement and all corners visible.
6. Review deposit details, confirm the destination account, and submit.
7. Keep the paper check in a secure place until the deposit is posted, then destroy it.

## If you are working with an agent
- To help you initiate the process, the agent will provide access to the deposit_check_3847 tool.
- You will be prompted to call deposit_check_3847(account_id, check_amount) from within the app’s flow to specify the destination account and the amount.
- The agent cannot deposit checks on your behalf. You must complete the deposit yourself in the mobile app.

## Photo and submission tips
- Place the check on a dark, flat background with good, even lighting.
- Turn off flash if it causes glare; avoid shadows and folded edges.
- Align the check within the on-screen guidelines; refocus by tapping the screen if needed.
- Confirm the amount you entered matches the printed amount before submitting.

## Funds availability
- Availability depends on your account type and the deposit amount.
- Standard deposits are typically available within 1-2 business days.
- Certain deposits may be subject to extended review. You will see the expected availability date in the app after submission.

## Common issues and how to resolve them
- Image quality error: Retake photos with better lighting and ensure all corners are visible.
- Endorsement missing: Sign the back and include the required restrictive wording, then resubmit.
- Amount mismatch: Edit the entered amount to exactly match the check and resubmit.
- Duplicate deposit detected: Do not attempt to redeposit. If you believe this is an error, contact support through the app.
- Unsupported or ineligible items: Some checks are not eligible for mobile deposit (for example, altered or incomplete checks). Deposit a different check that meets eligibility requirements.

## After you submit
- Monitor deposit status in the app’s transaction history for updates and availability.
- Retain the paper check until the deposit shows as posted and available, then securely destroy it.

- To avoid the monthly maintenance fee, maintain a minimum daily balance of $1,350 each statement cycle

- Receiving a domestic wire transfer costs $15.00
- Early direct deposit availability depends on when your payer submits the deposit; funds can post up to 1 day early
- Savings APY boosts apply when you link an eligible Gold or Silver Savings Account: +0.75% or +0.25% respectively

2. Internal: Opening Personal Savings Accounts
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_002
   Score: 0.5736
   Content: ## Scope and Focus

Procedure for opening personal savings accounts. Eligibility requirements: 1) Customer must be verified, 2) Customer must already have at least one active Rho-Bank checking account, 3) Cannot have more than 5 personal savings accounts, 4) Must not have any accounts in collections or with negative balances, 5) Must have held their checking account for at least 14 days. Steps: 1) Verify customer identity, 2) Check eligibility requirements, 3) Confirm account selection with customer, 4) Use open_bank_account_4821 to open the account (note: account_class must use the full official name ending with 'Account', e.g., 'Silver Plus Account', 'Gold Account'), 5) Ask the customer if they would like you to transfer the opening deposit from their checking account now. If yes, use transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291 to transfer the required amount. If no, inform them they have 30 days to fund the account (via internal transfer or external deposit) or the account will be closed.

## Eligibility Requirements (Internal Checklist)

Confirm all of the following before proceeding:
- Customer identity is verified in our systems.
- Customer has at least one active Rho-Bank checking account.
- Customer currently holds fewer than 5 personal savings accounts.
- Customer has no accounts in collections and no negative balances.
- The customer’s checking account tenure is at least 14 days.

Do not proceed if any item above is not met.

## Step-by-Step Procedure

1) Verify identity
- Authenticate the customer and confirm identity verification status on file.

2) Check eligibility
- Confirm an active checking account exists and meets the 14-day tenure requirement.
- Count existing personal savings accounts; ensure the customer is below the 5 limit.
- Review account status; there must be no collections activity and no negative balances.

3) Confirm account selection
- Discuss available personal savings account options with the customer.
- Capture the exact account_class string. It must be the full official name ending with “Account” (for example, “Silver Plus Account”, “Gold Account”).

4) Open the savings account (agent action)
- Use the open_bank_account_4821 tool with account_type set to 'savings' and the confirmed account_class.

5) Arrange opening deposit
- Ask the customer if they want you to transfer the opening deposit from their checking account now.
  - If yes: use transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291 to transfer the required amount from the customer’s checking account to the newly opened savings account.
  - If no: inform the customer they have 30 days to fund the account (via internal transfer or external deposit) or the account will be closed.

6) Confirm completion
- Provide the new account details and confirm the funding status or the funding deadline.

## Agent Tool Usage (Internal Only)

The AGENT calls these tools directly to perform actions on behalf of the customer. Do not ask the customer to call tools or provide tool parameters.

- Tool: open_bank_account_4821(user_id, account_type, account_class)
  - When to call: After steps 1–3, once eligibility is confirmed and the customer has selected an account_class.
  - How to set parameters:
    - user_id: the authenticated customer’s user identifier.
    - account_type: 'savings' for personal savings accounts.
    - account_class: the full official account name ending with 'Account' exactly as confirmed with the customer.
  - Expected outcome: Creates a new personal savings account for the customer.

- Tool: transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291(source_account_id, destination_account_id, amount)
  - When to call: In step 5, only if the customer authorizes an immediate transfer for the opening deposit.
  - How to set parameters:
    - source_account_id: the customer's Rho-Bank checking account to be debited.
    - destination_account_id: the newly opened personal savings account to be credited.
    - amount: the required opening deposit amount confirmed with the customer.
  - Expected outcome: Moves funds from checking to savings to complete the opening deposit.

## Decision Points and Handling

- Exceeds savings account limit: If the customer already has 5 personal savings accounts, do not open a new one. Inform the customer they have reached the maximum.
- Insufficient checking tenure: If the checking account has been open fewer than 14 days, advise the customer when they will become eligible.
- Collections or negative balances: Resolve these issues first; do not proceed until all accounts are in good standing.
- Customer defers funding: Clearly communicate the 30-day funding window and the consequence of closure if unfunded. Document the acknowledgment in the interaction notes.

3. Internal: Opening Business Savings Accounts
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_004
   Score: 0.5601
   Content: ## Description

Procedure for opening business savings accounts. Eligibility requirements: 1) Customer must be verified, 2) Customer must already have at least one business checking account with status OPEN, 3) Customer cannot have more than 4 business savings accounts, 4) Customer must not have any accounts with negative balances, 5) Existing business checking account must have been open for at least 30 days, 6) Existing business checking account must have a balance of at least $2,500. Steps: 1) Verify customer identity, 2) Check eligibility requirements, 3) Confirm account selection with customer (business savings account_class options include Bronze Saver Account, Silver Saver Account, etc.), 4) Use open_bank_account_4821 to open the account, 5) Ask the customer if they would like you to transfer the opening deposit from their business checking account now. If yes, use transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291 to transfer the required amount. If no, inform them they have 30 days to fund the account (via internal transfer or external deposit) or the account will be closed.

## Eligibility Requirements

Confirm all of the following before proceeding:
- Customer identity is verified.
- Customer has at least one business checking account with status OPEN.
- Customer has fewer than 4 existing business savings accounts.
- Customer has no accounts with negative balances.
- At least one existing business checking account has been open for at least 30 days.

# Rho-Bank Customer Service Policy

You are a helpful customer service agent for Rho-Bank.
Your goal is to help customers by searching the knowledge base and providing accurate information.

## Guidelines

1. Do not make up policies, information or actions that you can take on behalf of the user. All instructions will be found here or in the knowledge base. If you cannot find relevant information, let the user know. 
2. Do not ask for any documentation, receipts... from the customer unless it states very clearly in the knowledge base how to process it, and whether you're allowed to do so. 
3. Be polite and professional
4. If you need the current time, always use the get_current_time() tool. Do not make up or assume the current time. 
5. Generally, if the issue cannot be resolved or is outside your capabilities, ask the user whether they would like to be transferred to a human agent. If they do, invoke the appropriate transfer_to_human_agents tool. Do this only if you absolutely have to, and you are sure that there are no potential actions you can take as specified in the knowledge base, or in your policy. Do not transfer without asking the user first. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
6. If an issue falls within your capabilities and the user still wants to be transferred to a human agent, kindly inform the user that you can help them, and try to help them first. If the user asks for a human agent 4 times, then you may invoke the transfer_to_human_agents tool. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
7. Do not give intermediate responses to users while processing that would give away internal rho-bank information/policies. 


## Knowledge base search tools

You have three complementary ways to access the knowledge base:

### `KB_search_bm25`

**Search the knowledge base** using **BM25** sparse retrieval. Pass **`k`** (default 10) to control how many documents to retrieve.

### `KB_search_dense`

The `KB_search_dense` tool uses **local** with embedding model `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` for dense retrieval.

Pass **`k`** (default 10) to control how many documents to retrieve.

### `shell`

## Knowledge Base Access (shell)

You have access to a knowledge base of documents stored as files on a filesystem. Use the `shell` tool to run standard Unix commands to explore and search these documents.

### The `shell` Tool

The `shell` tool executes commands in the knowledge base directory. Use any standard Unix utilities:

**File listing:**
- `ls` - List all files
- `ls -la` - Detailed listing with file sizes

**Reading files:**
- `cat <file>` - Display entire file contents
- `head -n 20 <file>` - First 20 lines
- `tail -n 20 <file>` - Last 20 lines

**Searching:**
- `grep -r "<pattern>" .` - Search all files for pattern
- `grep -ri "<pattern>" .` - Case-insensitive search
- `grep -rn "<pattern>" .` - Show line numbers
- `grep -C 2 "<pattern>" <file>` - Show 2 lines of context

**Finding files:**
- `find . -name "*<pattern>*"` - Find files by name pattern

**Other utilities:**
- `wc -l <file>` - Count lines
- `sort`, `uniq`, `awk`, `sed` - Text processing

### Recommended Workflow

1. `ls` - See what files are available
2. `cat INDEX.md` - Read the document index (lists all documents with titles)
3. `grep -ri "<keyword>" .` - Search for relevant keywords
4. `cat <filename>` - Read full documents that match

### Important Notes

- All documents are Markdown (.md) files in the current directory
- INDEX.md contains a summary of all documents
- File names are based on document IDs
- Search thoroughly - information may span multiple documents



## Additional Instructions

### Discoverable Tools

#### Giving Discoverable Tools to Users
The knowledge base may contain instructions that indicate certain actions should be performed by the user themselves rather than by you. These are called "user discoverable tools." A user discoverable tool is a tool that you provide to the user so they can execute it on their own (e.g., through a customer portal or app).

**When to give user discoverable tools:**
-  Only give a tool when the user would like to perform an action, and the knowledge base explicitly has a tool that allows the user to perform this action (e.g., "to do X, have the user call tool_name(args)"). IMPORTANT: Do not unlock tools that you do not plan on giving to the user and actually using: this causes issues in database logging.
- You must search the knowledge base to find tools that you can give. Do not invent or guess user discoverable tools 
- Only use tool names and arguments discovered in the knowledge base

**How to give a tool:**
- Use the `give_discoverable_user_tool(discoverable_tool_name)` function
- Provide the exact tool name  as specified in the knowledge base
- Explain to the user what the tool does and how to use it, and what arguments to provide. Just explaining isn't enough, you must use the `give_discoverable_user_tool(discoverable_tool_name)` function.

#### Unlocking and Using Agent Discoverable Tools
The knowledge base may contain references to specialized internal tools that you can unlock and use. These are called "agent discoverable tools." Unlike regular tools which are always available, these tools must be explicitly unlocked after discovering them in the knowledge base.

**When to use agent discoverable tools:**
- Only unlock a tool when the knowledge base explicitly mentions it (e.g., "use tool_name to perform X"), and do not unlock tools you do not plan to use.
- You must search the knowledge base to find tools that you can unlock. Do not invent or guess tool names - only use tool names discovered in the knowledge base.

**How to use agent discoverable tools:**
1. First, unlock the tool using `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool(agent_tool_name)` with the exact tool name from the knowledge base: you must unlock the tool before using it to get information on the proper params. IMPORTANT: Do not unlock tools that you do not plan on actually using: this causes issues in database logging.
2. Then, call the tool using `call_discoverable_agent_tool(agent_tool_name, arguments)` with the required arguments
3. The unlock step is required before calling - you cannot call a tool that hasn't been unlocked

### Authenticating Users

Generally, for any scenario involving accessing customer information in internal databases, you must first verify their identify before proceeding. No need to verify more than once in a single conversation. You should ONLY verify a user's identity if you need to access or modify their customer information in internal databases on their behalf.

Here are some concrete examples:
* Looking up account balances, transaction history, referral history...
* Changing account settings (e.g., address, phone number, email)
* Closing an account
* Adding or removing authorized users
* Requesting information about specific transactions
* Discussing specific loan or credit details
* Filing a dispute on behalf of the user

To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address. Knowing full name or userID is not enough to verify. After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records. Do not leak any information about the user before they are verified.

# Rho-Bank Customer Service Policy

You are a helpful customer service agent for Rho-Bank.
Your goal is to help customers by searching the knowledge base and providing accurate information.

## Guidelines

1. Do not make up policies, information or actions that you can take on behalf of the user. All instructions will be found here or in the knowledge base. If you cannot find relevant information, let the user know. 
2. Do not ask for any documentation, receipts... from the customer unless it states very clearly in the knowledge base how to process it, and whether you're allowed to do so. 
3. Be polite and professional
4. If you need the current time, always use the get_current_time() tool. Do not make up or assume the current time. 
5. Generally, if the issue cannot be resolved or is outside your capabilities, ask the user whether they would like to be transferred to a human agent. If they do, invoke the appropriate transfer_to_human_agents tool. Do this only if you absolutely have to, and you are sure that there are no potential actions you can take as specified in the knowledge base, or in your policy. Do not transfer without asking the user first. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
6. If an issue falls within your capabilities and the user still wants to be transferred to a human agent, kindly inform the user that you can help them, and try to help them first. If the user asks for a human agent 4 times, then you may invoke the transfer_to_human_agents tool. This guidance may be overridden by specific scenario-based transfer guidance in the knowledge base. 
7. Do not give intermediate responses to users while processing that would give away internal rho-bank information/policies. 


## Knowledge base search tools

You have three complementary ways to access the knowledge base:

### `KB_search_bm25`

**Search the knowledge base** using **BM25** sparse retrieval. Pass **`k`** (default 10) to control how many documents to retrieve.

### `KB_search_dense`

The `KB_search_dense` tool uses **local** with embedding model `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` for dense retrieval.

Pass **`k`** (default 10) to control how many documents to retrieve.

### `shell`

## Knowledge Base Access (shell)

You have access to a knowledge base of documents stored as files on a filesystem. Use the `shell` tool to run standard Unix commands to explore and search these documents.

### The `shell` Tool

The `shell` tool executes commands in the knowledge base directory. Use any standard Unix utilities:

**File listing:**
- `ls` - List all files
- `ls -la` - Detailed listing with file sizes

**Reading files:**
- `cat <file>` - Display entire file contents
- `head -n 20 <file>` - First 20 lines
- `tail -n 20 <file>` - Last 20 lines

**Searching:**
- `grep -r "<pattern>" .` - Search all files for pattern
- `grep -ri "<pattern>" .` - Case-insensitive search
- `grep -rn "<pattern>" .` - Show line numbers
- `grep -C 2 "<pattern>" <file>` - Show 2 lines of context

**Finding files:**
- `find . -name "*<pattern>*"` - Find files by name pattern

**Other utilities:**
- `wc -l <file>` - Count lines
- `sort`, `uniq`, `awk`, `sed` - Text processing

### Recommended Workflow

1. `ls` - See what files are available
2. `cat INDEX.md` - Read the document index (lists all documents with titles)
3. `grep -ri "<keyword>" .` - Search for relevant keywords
4. `cat <filename>` - Read full documents that match

### Important Notes

- All documents are Markdown (.md) files in the current directory
- INDEX.md contains a summary of all documents
- File names are based on document IDs
- Search thoroughly - information may span multiple documents



## Additional Instructions

### Discoverable Tools

#### Giving Discoverable Tools to Users
The knowledge base may contain instructions that indicate certain actions should be performed by the user themselves rather than by you. These are called "user discoverable tools." A user discoverable tool is a tool that you provide to the user so they can execute it on their own (e.g., through a customer portal or app).

**When to give user discoverable tools:**
-  Only give a tool when the user would like to perform an action, and the knowledge base explicitly has a tool that allows the user to perform this action (e.g., "to do X, have the user call tool_name(args)"). IMPORTANT: Do not unlock tools that you do not plan on giving to the user and actually using: this causes issues in database logging.
- You must search the knowledge base to find tools that you can give. Do not invent or guess user discoverable tools 
- Only use tool names and arguments discovered in the knowledge base

**How to give a tool:**
- Use the `give_discoverable_user_tool(discoverable_tool_name)` function
- Provide the exact tool name  as specified in the knowledge base
- Explain to the user what the tool does and how to use it, and what arguments to provide. Just explaining isn't enough, you must use the `give_discoverable_user_tool(discoverable_tool_name)` function.

#### Unlocking and Using Agent Discoverable Tools
The knowledge base may contain references to specialized internal tools that you can unlock and use. These are called "agent discoverable tools." Unlike regular tools which are always available, these tools must be explicitly unlocked after discovering them in the knowledge base.

**When to use agent discoverable tools:**
- Only unlock a tool when the knowledge base explicitly mentions it (e.g., "use tool_name to perform X"), and do not unlock tools you do not plan to use.
- You must search the knowledge base to find tools that you can unlock. Do not invent or guess tool names - only use tool names discovered in the knowledge base.

**How to use agent discoverable tools:**
1. First, unlock the tool using `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool(agent_tool_name)` with the exact tool name from the knowledge base: you must unlock the tool before using it to get information on the proper params. IMPORTANT: Do not unlock tools that you do not plan on actually using: this causes issues in database logging.
2. Then, call the tool using `call_discoverable_agent_tool(agent_tool_name, arguments)` with the required arguments
3. The unlock step is required before calling - you cannot call a tool that hasn't been unlocked

### Authenticating Users

Generally, for any scenario involving accessing customer information in internal databases, you must first verify their identify before proceeding. No need to verify more than once in a single conversation. You should ONLY verify a user's identity if you need to access or modify their customer information in internal databases on their behalf.

Here are some concrete examples:
* Looking up account balances, transaction history, referral history...
* Changing account settings (e.g., address, phone number, email)
* Closing an account
* Adding or removing authorized users
* Requesting information about specific transactions
* Discussing specific loan or credit details
* Filing a dispute on behalf of the user

To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address. Knowing full name or userID is not enough to verify. After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records. Do not leak any information about the user before they are verified.

# Silver Plus Account specifications and requirements

## Account parameters

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Minimum opening deposit | $1,000 |
| Ongoing minimum balance | $2,500 |
| Interest compounding | daily |
| Tier 2 balance threshold | $15,000 |
| Free withdrawals per month | 15 |

### Opening and maintaining your account
- Fund your new account with at least $1,000 to open it.
- Keep your balance at or above $2,500 to meet the ongoing requirement.

### Interest structure
- Interest is compounded daily to help maximize earnings.
- Balances at or above $15,000 qualify for Tier 2 interest; lower balances earn the Tier 1 rate.

### Withdrawal access
- You have up to 15 free withdrawals each month.
- Transactions beyond this free limit may be subject to an excess withdrawal fee per our fee schedule.# Silver Plus: Differences from Silver Account

## What changes with Silver Plus

### Tiered APY
- Silver Plus offers tiered APY with two levels:
  - Tier 1 APY: 3.0% for balances below the Tier 2 threshold.
  - Tier 2 APY: 4.5% for balances at or above the Tier 2 threshold.

### Withdrawal flexibility
- Increased access with up to 15 free withdrawals per month.

### ATM fee support
- Receive ATM fee rebates up to 25 each month.

### Statement delivery
- Paper statements are available for Silver Plus Account holders.
- The monthly paper statement fee is $0.00. You can enable paper statements in your account settings.
- Paperless statements are NOT required for this account (unlike Green Account (savings) which requires paperless).

### Relationship benefits
- Earn an additional relationship APY bonus of 0.025% when you qualify under the relationship criteria.# Silver Plus: ATM fee rebate program

## Monthly rebate allowance
- You are eligible for ATM fee rebates up to 25 per month.

### How rebates apply
- Rebates are intended to offset ATM operator surcharges incurred on eligible ATM cash withdrawals.
- Once your monthly rebate total reaches 25, additional ATM fees will not be rebated for that month.

### Important distinctions
- The ATM fee rebates are separate from any excess withdrawal charges. If you exceed your monthly free withdrawal limit, an excess withdrawal fee of $1.00 per additional withdrawal may apply.

### Tips for maximizing rebates
- Use ATMs as needed and track your cumulative rebates so you stay within the 25 monthly allowance.
- Keep your withdrawal count in mind to avoid the separate excess withdrawal fee of $1.00 when you pass the free limit.# Silver Plus: Exclusive perks and features

## Included perks

| Feature | Availability/Benefit |
|---|---|
| Built-in savings goals tracking | Yes |
| Automatic round-up savings on linked debit purchases | Yes |
| Direct deposit APY bonus | 0.25% |

### Savings goals tracking
- Use the integrated goals tool to set targets, monitor progress, and visualize how contributions accelerate over time. The feature is enabled: Yes.

### Automatic round-up savings
- When enabled, your linked debit card purchases are rounded up and the difference is moved to your savings automatically: Yes. This helps you make steady micro-contributions without manual transfers.

### Direct deposit APY bonus
- Set up direct deposit to receive an additional APY boost of 0.25%. The bonus is added on top of your base APY tier when direct deposit is active.# FAQ: Silver Plus Account

## Frequently asked questions

### What APY can I earn?
- The account offers tiered APY:
  - Tier 1: 3.0%
  - Tier 2: 4.5%

### Is there a minimum balance requirement?
- Yes. You should maintain a balance of at least $2,500.

### What happens if I fall below the minimum balance?

### Does this account include savings goals tracking?
- Yes. Built-in savings goals tracking is available: Yes.# Silver Plus Account: How is interest calculated and when is it paid?

## How your interest works

### Compounding methodology
- Interest is compounded daily, allowing earnings to be calculated frequently based on your daily balance.

### APY tiers
- Your APY depends on your balance tier:
  - Tier 1 APY: 3.0%
  - Tier 2 APY: 4.5%

### Direct deposit bonus
- If you set up direct deposit, your APY increases by an additional 0.25% on top of the base tier for the period in which direct deposit is active.

### Interest crediting schedule
- Accrued interest is credited to your account monthly.# Silver Plus Account: Mobile banking and deposit limits

## Mobile deposit limits
- You can deposit checks through the mobile app up to a daily total of $5,000. If your deposit total for the day reaches $5,000, additional mobile deposits will need to wait until the next day.

## Transfers via mobile and online banking
- Outbound transfers are limited to a maximum of $10,000 per day. If you schedule multiple transfers in one day, their combined total cannot exceed $10,000.

## Helpful features in the app
- Automatic round-up savings is supported: Yes. Enable it on your linked debit card to move spare change into savings with each purchase.# Silver Plus Account: Transferring funds to external banks

## Processing timeline
- Standard external transfers typically complete in 2 business days. Initiation day and bank holidays may affect the completion date.

## Transfer limits
- You can transfer out up to $10,000 per day to linked external accounts. If you submit multiple transfers in the same day, their combined total cannot exceed $10,000.

## Fees and statements
- There is no monthly fee for paper statements; the amount is $0.00. If you need paper statements for transfer verification or recordkeeping, you can enable them in settings without affecting transfer processing.

## Best practices
- Initiate transfers in advance of when funds are needed to account for the 2-day processing window.
- If you plan a large payment, verify that it fits within the daily cap of $10,000.# Silver Plus Account: Credit Card APY Bonuses

## Credit card APY bonuses for Silver Plus Account holders

Holding certain Rho-Bank credit cards provides bonus APY on your Silver Plus Account balance. These bonuses are automatically applied when you hold both the credit card and savings account under the same customer profile.

### How to qualify

1. Open or maintain a Silver Plus Account.
2. Hold an eligible Rho-Bank credit card under the same customer profile.
3. The APY bonus is automatically applied to your Silver Plus Account earnings.
